name: Acute Sensory Ataxic Neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Acute Sensory Ataxic Neuropathy

criteria.description: Rapid onset of sensory ataxia developing over days to weeks
Predominant involvement of large sensory fibers with loss of proprioception and vibration sense
Electrophysiological evidence of sensory neuropathy with preserved motor nerve function
Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein without pleocytosis
Exclusion of other causes of sensory ataxia such as vitamin deficiencies, toxins, or hereditary neuropathies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (acute onset sensory ataxia, predominant large sensory fiber involvement, and electrophysiological evidence) with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: CSF analysis and exclusion of mimics are important to support diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe sensory ataxia with impaired proprioception
searchTerms: severe balance problems from sensory loss
marked sensory ataxia with poor position sense
difficulty walking due to proprioception loss

pathognomonic.symptomName: Loss of vibration sense in distal limbs
searchTerms: loss of vibration feeling in hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Areflexia or hyporeflexia in affected limbs

searchTerms: pins and needles in distal extremities

common.symptomName: Gait instability due to sensory loss
searchTerms: unsteady walking due to sensory loss
balance issues from sensory nerve damage
positive balance test with eyes closed
difficulty standing steady with eyes shut
mild numbness in hands and feet

occasional.symptomName: Mild distal weakness secondary to disuse
searchTerms: mild weakness in distal muscles from inactivity
slight muscle loss due to disuse
weakness in hands or feet from lack of use
unpleasant abnormal sensations in hands or feet

occasional.symptomName: Autonomic symptoms such as orthostatic hypotension
searchTerms: autonomic symptoms like dizziness on standing
mild sensory nerve problems in face or head
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein without pleocytosis
Normal vitamin B12 and folate levels
imaging: Normal brain and spinal cord MRI excluding central causes
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; typically sporadic
other: Nerve conduction studies showing absent or reduced sensory nerve action potentials with preserved motor responses

distinguishingFeatures: Motor weakness prominent in Guillain-Barré syndrome
Rapid progression with possible respiratory failure
MRI may show spinal cord involvement

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness or respiratory compromise
Signs of central nervous system involvement
references: Dalakas MC. Acute sensory ataxic neuropathy: clinical and electrophysiological features. Neurology. 1990.
Hadden RD, et al. Diagnostic criteria for Guillain-Barré syndrome and related disorders. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 2010.
